title: People Ops — Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Playbook (2026)
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's standard operating procedures for: hiring, candidate selection, employee onboarding (pre-boarding through 90 days), performance and feedback cycles, and manager guidance for running these processes consistently and fairly. It is the canonical reference for hiring managers, interviewers, and people-ops partners.

Key principles
- Candidate experience first: timely communications, clear expectations, and respectful interview loops.
- Consistency: scorecards, rubrics, and calibration prevent bias and maintain hiring bar.
- Speed with quality: meet SLA targets while prioritizing quality-of-hire.
- Manager enablement: provide templates, checklists, and signposts so managers focus on technical/role fit rather than process mechanics.

Tools and systems
- ATS: Greenhouse (primary). All job postings, stage moves, interviewer feedback, and scorecards must be recorded in Greenhouse.
- HRIS: Workday (employee record, payroll, benefits).
- Identity & access: Okta + 1Password for secrets.
- Communication: Slack (people-ops channel #people-ops, hiring-specific private channels per role).
- Learning: Lattice (performance reviews), Confluence (policy docs).

Hiring process (end-to-end)
1) Requisition & approval
  - Manager creates a requisition in Greenhouse and requests headcount approval in Workday.
  - Required approvals: manager -> director -> finance (if > $150k comp) -> people-ops.
  - SLA: approvals should complete within 3 business days.

2) Sourcing & outreach
  - Responsible: hiring manager + recruiting partner.
  - Channels: internal referrals, inbound candidates, LinkedIn, recruiting agencies (used sparingly), career site.
  - Diversity goal: ensure final interview slate includes at least one candidate from an underrepresented group when feasible.

3) Screening & interviews
  - Phone screen (30m): recruiter screens for compensation, basic qualifications, and alignment. Use screening template in Greenhouse.
  - Hiring manager screen (30-45m): high-level role fit.
  - Technical interview(s): role-specific technical assessments. Use standardized rubrics.
  - Behavioral interview (45m): culture add/leadership.
  - Cross-functional partner interview (30-45m): collaboration and judgment.
  - On-site / virtual loop: ideally 3-5 interviews in one day or spread across 2 days.
  - Interviewer expectations: submit feedback & scorecard in Greenhouse within 24 hours of interview.

Interview scorecards & decision criteria
- Use role-specific scorecards stored in Greenhouse. Score components include: core skills, problem solving, collaboration, communication, and role-specific competencies.
- Pass thresholds: candidates should meet or exceed the hiring bar on 3 of 5 core dimensions and have no fail on safety/ethics questions.
- Disqualifiers: dishonesty in work history, inability to communicate key role responsibilities, failing background check.

Decision & offer
- Hiring manager synthesizes feedback into a hiring recommendation.
- Offer approvals required: hiring manager, people-ops partner, and finance (if comp > $150k).
- Offer process SLA: time-to-offer target is 14 calendar days from first interview.
- Offer components: base salary, equity (if applicable), sign-on (if applicable), start date, benefits summary, relocation (if applicable).
- Background checks: initiated immediately after verbal offer; expected completion within 3 business days.

Metrics and targets (people-ops KPIs)
- Time-to-offer: target 14 days (median).
- Time-to-fill: target 45 days (median from requisition approval to start date).
- Offer acceptance rate: target >= 75%.
- Interview-to-offer conversion: target ~20%.
- Referral-to-hire ratio: target 25% of hires from referrals.

Onboarding (pre-boarding through 90 days)
Pre-boarding (before start date)
- People-ops tasks: start paperwork in Workday, set up payroll, benefits enrollment instructions sent, background check verification, contractor agreement if applicable.
- Hiring manager tasks: email welcome note, send first-week agenda, assign 30-60-90 plan template, request equipment and access via IT ticket tool.
- IT tasks: provision laptop, corporate email, Okta account, 1Password vault, Slack invite, calendar invites for first week.

Day 0 (first day)
- HR welcome (30-45m): benefits overview, HR policies, security training assignment.
- Manager 1:1 (60m): role context, team overview, immediate priorities.
- Equipment validation: confirm laptop, access, and internal tooling.
- Buddy pairing: assign a buddy for the first 30 days.

First week
- Product/tech orientation sessions: architecture overview, codebase walkthroughs, service maps.
- Role-specific training: onboarding tasks in the repo, required readings.
- 1:1s scheduled weekly with manager.

30-60-90 day plan (template)
- 30 days: get productive on smaller scoped tasks, pass code reviews, complete required trainings, meet >10 cross-functional partners.
- 60 days: lead one medium-scope project, contribute to team rituals, demonstrate ownership of at least one service.
- 90 days: own a customer-impacting area, present a 90-day retrospective + plan for next 6 months.

Onboarding checklist (required items)
- Workday record completed
- Payroll and tax forms submitted
- Benefits enrollment started
- Okta/1Password provisioned
- Slack, email, and calendar access
- Local development environment running (if engineering)
- Security & compliance training completed
- Team intro documented in Confluence

Performance & feedback cycles
Overview
- Redwood uses a continuous feedback culture supported by scheduled reviews. Formal cycles are: mid-year checkpoint and year-end review (Lattice). Managers should also run quarterly 1:1s and monthly skip-levels as appropriate.

Cadence and mechanics
- Weekly 1:1s: focused on priorities, roadblocks, and feedback.
- Quarterly goals: set at team level, aligned to company themes.
- Mid-year checkpoint: informal calibration, adjustment of goals, and career conversation.
- Year-end review: formal performance rating, calibration, and comp decisions.

Performance ratings & calibration
- Rating scale: Exceeds Expectations | Meets Expectations | Needs Improvement.
- Managers must provide at least 2 examples of impact for any rating other than Meets Expectations.
- Calibration process: managers submit recommended ratings with written rationale; calibration committee (managers + HRBP) reviews across teams to ensure equity.

Feedback best practices for managers
- Be timely: deliver feedback within 48 hours of a notable event when possible.
- Be specific: describe behavior, impact, and suggested next steps (Situation-Behavior-Impact).
- Balance: provide both strengths and growth areas.
- Ask & listen: create space for the employee's perspective and agreement on action items.

Performance improvement plans (PIPs)
- Use when an employee is consistently rated Needs Improvement and prior coaching has not resulted in change.
- PIP components: specific objectives, measurable success criteria, timeline (typically 60-90 days), resources and manager support, weekly check-ins, and clear consequences.
- Ownership: manager drafts PIP with HRBP review and sign-off.

Promotion & leveling guidance (summary)
- Promotion readiness checklist: consistent performance at higher level expectations, documented impact across multiple quarters, manager & peer support, and cross-team influence.
- Compensation adjustments: recommended by manager, reviewed by people-ops and finance.
- Promotion approvals: manager -> director -> HRBP -> leveling committee.

Manager playbook — interviewing & hiring
Interviewer training
- Mandatory: all interviewers must complete annual interviewer training (bias awareness, structured interviewing, scorecard use). Training records are tracked by people-ops.

Structuring interview loops
- Minimum required roles for IC hiring: 1 hiring manager interview, 2 technical interviews, 1 behavioral/collaboration interview.
- Keep loops efficient: avoid >5 interviews unless exceptional circumstances.

Running an effective debrief
- Timeline: schedule hiring debrief within 24 hours of final interview.
- Preparation: interviewer feedback submitted in Greenhouse.
- Decision criteria: align on scorecard, go/no-go thresholds, and candidate fit.

Compensation conversations
- Do not discuss compensation specifics publicly. Only people-ops and the hiring manager should handle fragile negotiations.
- For counteroffers: consult people-ops. Use market data from our comp band spreadsheet maintained by finance/people-ops.

Manager playbook — coaching & development
Career conversations
- Frequency: formal career conversation at least once per quarter.
- Topics: growth goals, skill gaps, stretch opportunities, mentorship. Document outcomes in Lattice or Confluence.

Development plans
- Create 90-day learning objectives with milestones, recommended resources (internal docs, relevant trainings, peer mentoring), and success criteria.

Sample templates (copy & paste)
Offer approval checklist (email subject: "Offer Approval — [Candidate Name] — [Role]")
- Candidate name: 
- Role & level: 
- Proposed base salary & equity: 
- Sign-on & relocation: 
- Hiring manager justification (3 bullet points): 
- Approvals: Manager, HRBP, Finance (if required)

First week agenda (Manager -> New hire)
- Day 1 AM: HR welcome & benefits (30m)
- Day 1 PM: Team intro + 1:1 with manager (60m)
- Day 2: Tech/product orientation (90m)
- Day 3: First small assignment & pairing sessions
- Day 4: Cross-functional intro meetings
- Day 5: 30-day goals alignment

Common FAQs
- Q: What if an interviewer misses feedback deadline?
  A: People-ops will ping the interviewer. Repeated misses trigger a coaching conversation with their manager.
- Q: Can we extend remote job offers to multiple regions?
  A: Check data residency & payroll constraints with finance/people-ops before extending offers outside US/EU.
